_meta.purpose: Hand-computed oracle fixtures for signals/premiums.py (§7.5), recorded per the M0 deliverable outstanding since 2026-07-31 (CLAUDE.md 'Current state'; §15; §16 M0 exit gate: 'the §7.5 worked FX example passes through the typed convert()'). This file is data only — no test code and no application code, since signals/premiums.py does not exist yet. A future pytest test (M2+) loads this file and asserts against it.
_meta.formula: foreign_price_usd = foreign_price_local * usd_per_foreign_currency; implied_us_price = foreign_price_usd * local_ordinary_shares_per_adr; premium_pct = (us_price / implied_us_price - 1) * 100  — §7.5 pseudocode. local_ordinary_shares_per_adr is the count of foreign ordinary shares one ADR represents, and it is ALWAYS the multiplier in that direction in every case below — it can be < 1 (SKHY: 0.1, one ADR is a tenth of a Korean share) or > 1 (TSM-style: 5, one ADR bundles five local shares), but the arithmetic never flips to division either way; only the magnitude changes. It is named directionally rather than a bare 'ratio' or 'adr_ratio' for the same reason ADR-0001 forbids a bare fx_rate: a plain scalar's direction has to be guessed, and guessing wrong produces a plausible-looking wrong number instead of a loud error.
_meta.adr_0001_alignment: usd_per_foreign_currency is always the ADR-0001 named quantity, never a bare fx_rate. Each case also records the raw provider-convention quoted_rate it was derived from, and that provider's quoting convention (e.g. 'KRW per USD', per the verified KRW=X finding), so an inversion is visible in the fixture itself rather than hidden behind the final number.
_meta.tolerance_rationale: expected.premium_pct in each case is the EXACT result of the stated formula on the stated inputs, computed independently of the spec's prose rounding. Case spec_worked_example's exact result is -3.348582% (as a fraction, -3660/1093), not -3.3% — the '-3.3%' in §7.5 line 491 is prose rounded for readability, not a second figure a correct implementation needs to hit. Because 'expected' here is already the precise value, tolerance_abs_pct only has to absorb floating-point representation noise from re-deriving the same arithmetic in a different order or language — not spec rounding. That's why the tolerances below are tight (1e-4 to 1e-9 absolute percentage points) rather than loose enough to swallow the ~0.049-point gap to the prose figure: a tolerance wide enough to accept -3.3% would also silently accept a real ~0.05-point calculation error, which defeats a fixture whose entire purpose (§15: 'MUST reproduce exactly') is to fail loudly on exactly that class of bug.

cases.description: Real (non-synthetic) M0 spike 1 evidence for the session-mismatch pairing case discussed in §7.5's spike-1 paragraph (line 486): NY close 2026-07-30 paired against Seoul close 2026-07-31, one calendar day apart, per the most-recent-close-to-most-recent-close pairing rule §7.5 decides on.
cases.source: spikes/spike1_evidence.json — values below are copied verbatim from that file, not independently re-derived, so this fixture can never drift from the actual spike run.
cases.warning: premium_pct here is +23.90%, an order of magnitude larger than a typical cross-listing premium. THIS IS NOT A CALCULATION BUG AND NOT ARBITRAGE. It is the measured cost of the pairing convention itself: the Seoul leg is one session newer than the NY leg (Seoul had already closed hours before this NY session opened). §7.5 documents the same underlying pair on date-aligned legs giving +61.01% instead — a 37-point swing from pairing choice alone, not from a calculation error. If a reproduction of this fixture yields anything other than ~+23.90%, that IS a bug. If a future reader is surprised to see +23.9% in 'premium' test data, they are seeing exactly the timing artifact §7.5 warns about, not a regression — do not 'fix' this fixture's value to look smaller.

inputs.quoted_rate_convention: KRW per USD (yfinance KRW=X direction, ADR-0001)

cases.arithmetic: foreign_price_usd = 600 * 0.03125 = 18.75; implied_us_price = 18.75 * 5 = 93.75 (multiply — same direction as the ratio-0.1 cases above: local_ordinary_shares_per_adr always multiplies foreign_price_usd, whether it is below 1 or above 1); premium_pct = (96.0 / 93.75 - 1) * 100 = 2.4 exactly
cases.note: premium_pct is an exact rational (2.4) by construction, unlike cases 1-2 which involve repeating decimals — a fast sanity fixture to trust before relying on the messier real-derived ones, and the one that most directly exercises local_ordinary_shares_per_adr > 1.
